claim: On one fixed eight-seed Ordon tactic-route workload, the runner used every requested persistent worker and preserved exact semantic results, but scaled to only 2.097x at eight workers. Efficiency fell from 73.7% at two workers to 26.2% at eight while peak memory reached 6.19 GB. The sweep disproves worker count as the only bottleneck: one run performs 320 small progressive native batches, and fixed validation plus worker startup consumes 49-58 seconds of the critical path.

workload.method: strong scaling of one fixed eight-seed campaign across 1, 2, 4, and 8 persistent native workers
workload.explanation: Each seed retained one 40-tick route tactic. The observation-driven route-sequence executor evaluated progressive prefixes of 1 through 40 ticks, totaling 820 candidate ticks and 40 native batch calls per seed. The fixed learning workload is therefore 6,560 evaluated ticks in 320 batches. Each additional persistent worker also pays a separate 160-tick authenticated initial probe; those setup ticks are reported separately and are not included in the fixed-work throughput rate.

measurement.outer_wall: Wall time from huntctl process launch through observed exit, including request and execution validation, artifact hashing, worker startup, initial probes, evaluation, persistence, and shutdown.
measurement.campaign_wall: Runner v7 wall time, beginning before configuration and execution-binding validation and ending immediately before final report encoding.
measurement.peak_tree_working_set: Maximum sampled sum of WorkingSet64 across huntctl and every descendant process.
measurement.restore: Sum of native checkpoint-restore phase measurements. Mean restore divides by every measured restore sample, including two validation restores per initial probe.
measurement.fixed_evaluation_native_ticks_per_second: The same 6,560 evaluated candidate ticks divided by outer wall time. It excludes worker-count-dependent initial-probe ticks.
measurement.useful_decisions_per_second: Eight useful retained decisions divided by outer wall time.
measurement.batch_wall: Sum of native batch-wall measurements. This is worker-time and therefore may exceed campaign wall when workers overlap.
measurement.semantic_identity: A canonical digest over every seed's success, decision count, episode count, route ticks, selection counts, selected option, reward, goal distances, terminal flag, endpoint snapshot identities, and player positions.

bottlenecks.fixed_startup: Configuration and execution validation, large-artifact hashing, concurrent worker startup, and authenticated initial probes consumed 49.4 seconds with one worker and 57.8 seconds with eight. At eight workers this was 75.6% of campaign wall.
bottlenecks.fine_grained_batches: Eight retained decisions expanded into 320 native calls because each 40-tick observation-driven route tactic replays prefixes 1 through 40. At one worker, native worker calls consumed 100.44 seconds while the native simulation phase itself consumed only 16.00 seconds. The gap is repeated restore, IPC, result validation, corpus production, and fixed batch overhead.
bottlenecks.contention: Summed native batch wall rose from 98.40 to 158.76 seconds; mean restore rose from 19.10 to 45.51 milliseconds; and summed seed wall rose from 111.28 to 146.45 seconds as worker count increased. More processes cannot repair this granularity and contention.
bottlenecks.rendering: CPU draw traversal and renderer submission were nested inside the simulation phase and together consumed 9.04 seconds at one worker. They matter, but even eliminating them impossibly for free would not explain the roughly 84 seconds between the internal simulation phase and native worker-call wall.
bottlenecks.persistence: Evidence projection and persistence grew from 3.33 to 5.15 seconds of worker-time and remained secondary to native call granularity and fixed startup.

recommendation.reason: Four workers are the current elbow: they improve useful throughput 86.5% over one worker at 2.30 GB additional peak memory. Eight workers add only 12.4% useful throughput over four while nearly doubling memory and increasing mean restore latency 79.5%.
recommendation.next_engineering_target: Replace the 40 progressively replayed one-candidate calls per route tactic with bounded equal-source tactic batches or a native observation-loop execution boundary, then rerun this exact sweep. Worker count alone cannot meet the P1 order-of-magnitude acceptance gate.
